title: IRAs: Roth vs Traditional
description: The account you open yourself, the dollar cap, and the income cap.
wolfLine: Under the limit, use the front door.

backdoor-roth.definition: A legal path some high earners use: a nondeductible traditional IRA contribution, then a conversion to a Roth IRA. If you already have pre-tax IRA money, the pro-rata rule can make part of the conversion taxable. This course names it. It does not walk the forms.
backdoor-roth.example: Income is over the Roth IRA limit, so a direct Roth contribution is not allowed.

steps.title: Not the workplace plan
steps.body: An IRA is an individual retirement account. You open it, not your employer. A [[traditional IRA|traditional-ira]] can give you a tax break now, if you qualify. A [[Roth IRA|roth-ira]] takes the tax break later, on a qualified withdrawal. The 2026 contribution limit is $7,500 for both of them combined, plus $1,100 if you are 50 or older.

steps.prompt: Who opens an IRA?
steps.explain: Individual means you. The 401(k) is the workplace one.

steps.prompt: What is the 2026 IRA contribution limit, in dollars, before the age-50 catch-up?
steps.explain: The 2026 limit is $7,500 across traditional and Roth IRAs combined.

steps.prompt: You can put $7,500 in a traditional IRA and another $7,500 in a Roth IRA in 2026.
steps.explain: The $7,500 is the total, split however you like between them. It is not $7,500 each.

steps.prompt: How is an IRA different from a 401(k)?
choices: The IRA is the account you open. The 401(k) comes from the job.
An IRA cannot hold a fund
steps.explain: Two containers. The limits are separate. The investments inside can look alike.

lessons.title: Roth or Traditional
lessons.summary: Now or later, and only if you qualify.

steps.title: The same $1,000, two doors
steps.body: If you can deduct a [[traditional IRA|traditional-ira]] contribution, $1,000 in the 12% bracket saves $120 this year. A [[Roth IRA|roth-ira]] saves $0 this year, and a qualified withdrawal of the earnings later is tax-free. The workplace-plan rules can shrink or erase the traditional deduction. The Roth door has its own income limit.

lines.label: Tax saved this year in the 12% bracket, if you can deduct it

steps.prompt: Which page can lower this year’s tax, if the deduction is allowed?
steps.explain: The traditional page is the deduction. $1,000 × 0.12 = $120. The Roth page pays the tax now.

steps.prompt: If the deduction is allowed, how many dollars of tax does $1,000 save in the 12% bracket?
steps.explain: $1,000 × 0.12 = $120. If the deduction is not allowed, that $120 does not happen.

steps.prompt: A Roth IRA contribution lowers this year’s taxable income.
steps.explain: Roth money was already taxed. The favor is on a qualified withdrawal later.

steps.prompt: You cannot deduct a traditional IRA, and your income is under the Roth limit. Which door is the simple one?
choices: Traditional, for a deduction you cannot take
Roth, since the traditional deduction is worth $0 here
Neither, so you skip retirement accounts
steps.explain: A nondeductible traditional contribution is the awkward one. Under the Roth limit, the Roth door is the direct one.

lessons.title: The 2026 IRA Limits
lessons.summary: The dollar cap, then the income cap.

steps.title: Two different gates
steps.body: The dollar gate: $7,500 in 2026, or $8,600 at age 50 or older. The income gate is for Roth IRAs. A single filer with modified AGI under $153,000 can make a full Roth contribution. At $168,000 or more, a direct Roth contribution is not allowed. Married filing jointly: full under $242,000, and none at $252,000 or more. This course will not compute a partial phase-out in between.

doc.title: 2026 IRA limits
doc.note: A single filer at $168,000 or more cannot make a direct Roth IRA contribution. A joint filer at $252,000 or more cannot. Under the start of the range, the full contribution is allowed.

steps.prompt: How many dollars can someone under 50 contribute to IRAs in 2026?
steps.explain: The base limit is $7,500, traditional and Roth combined.

doc.title: 2026 IRA limits
doc.note: A single filer at $168,000 or more cannot make a direct Roth IRA contribution. A joint filer at $252,000 or more cannot. Under the start of the range, the full contribution is allowed.

steps.prompt: How many dollars is the total at age 50 or older in 2026?
A single filer with modified AGI of $170,000 can make a direct Roth IRA contribution in 2026.
steps.explain: $170,000 is over $168,000. The direct Roth contribution is not allowed. A partial amount between $153,000 and $168,000 is a real thing, and this course does not grade that math.

steps.prompt: A single filer with modified AGI of $100,000 is under the 2026 Roth IRA income limit.
steps.explain: $100,000 is under $153,000, so the full Roth contribution is allowed, up to the $7,500 dollar cap and up to earned income.

lessons.title: Opening One
lessons.summary: Four steps, then leave it alone.

steps.title: The order
steps.body: You need earned income, such as wages. You check the limit that applies to you. Then you open the IRA, link a bank account, pick a [[fund]], and set an automatic transfer. The account is the container. The fund is what you own inside it.

steps.prompt: Put the opening in order.
items: Check that you have earned income and that the limit allows it
Choose a fund and set the automatic transfer
steps.explain: The limit first, so you do not contribute money you are not allowed to. The fund is last, and then the transfer repeats.

steps.prompt: What do you actually own inside the IRA?
choices: The IRA itself is the investment
The fund, or other investments, you buy in it
steps.explain: The IRA is the container. A broad, cheap fund is a solid thing to put in it.

steps.prompt: You can contribute more than you earned from work.
steps.explain: The IRA contribution cannot top your earned income, and it cannot top the yearly dollar limit.

steps.prompt: Maya earned $28,000 from work in 2026 and is under 50. What is the most she can contribute to IRAs, in dollars?
steps.explain: Her wages are over $7,500, and she is under 50, so the dollar cap is the binding one: $7,500.

steps.title: Both, if the rules allow
steps.body: The 2026 employee [[401(k)|401k]] limit is $24,500. The IRA limit is a separate $7,500. Using the workplace plan does not by itself ban an IRA. It can affect whether a traditional IRA contribution is deductible. A Roth IRA still has its income limit.

steps.prompt: In 2026, a 30-year-old puts $24,500 in a 401(k) and $7,500 in a Roth IRA. How many dollars went into retirement accounts?
steps.explain: $24,500 + $7,500 = $32,000. The two limits are separate, so this is allowed if the Roth income test is met and the person earned enough.

steps.prompt: Someone puts $2,000 in a Roth IRA and wants the rest of the 2026 IRA limit in a traditional IRA. How many dollars are left?
Maxing a 401(k) uses up the IRA limit too.
steps.explain: They are different limits. $24,500 at work does not reduce the $7,500 IRA cap.

steps.prompt: You have a 401(k) at work and your income is under the Roth IRA limit. What can you also do?
choices: Contribute to a Roth IRA, up to the IRA limit
Skip the employer match so the IRA is allowed
steps.explain: The match stays. The IRA is an extra container, inside its own limit.

lessons.title: The Backdoor, Named Only
lessons.summary: A high earner’s path. Not a worksheet.

steps.title: What the name means
steps.body: If your income is over the [[Roth IRA|roth-ira]] limit, a direct Roth contribution is not allowed. A [[backdoor Roth|backdoor-roth]] is a nondeductible contribution to a [[traditional IRA|traditional-ira]], followed by a conversion into a Roth IRA. If you already have pre-tax money in any traditional IRA, the pro-rata rule can tax part of that conversion. This lesson names the path. The forms and the tax math belong with the IRS or a tax pro, not in a quiz.

steps.prompt: Who is a backdoor Roth even about?
choices: Someone under the Roth income limit
Someone whose income is too high for a direct Roth IRA contribution
steps.explain: Under the limit, you just contribute to the Roth. The backdoor is for the person who cannot.

steps.prompt: A backdoor Roth is a way to skip taxes entirely, even if you have a large pre-tax IRA.
steps.explain: The pro-rata rule can make part of the conversion taxable when pre-tax IRA money already exists.

steps.prompt: What will this course not do?
choices: Walk the forms and compute a partial conversion
steps.explain: Naming it is the lesson. The worksheet is not.

steps.prompt: The rule that can tax part of the conversion when other traditional IRA money exists is the ___ rule.
steps.explain: Pro-rata. It looks at all your traditional IRAs, not only the new dollars.

lessons.title: Taking Money Out Early
lessons.summary: Contributions and earnings are not the same.

steps.title: Roth contributions are the flexible part
steps.body: You can usually withdraw your own [[Roth IRA|roth-ira]] contributions at any time, without tax or penalty. The earnings are the restricted part: generally tax-free only after age 59½ and a five-year clock, with some exceptions this course will not list as a plan. A [[traditional IRA|traditional-ira]] withdrawal before 59½ is usually income tax plus a 10% penalty.

steps.prompt: You contributed $2,000 to a Roth IRA. It is now worth $2,500. How many dollars are contributions you can usually take out?
steps.explain: The $2,000 is contributions. The other $500 is earnings, and those have the extra rules.

steps.prompt: How many dollars of that account are earnings?
A traditional IRA withdrawal at age 40 is usually tax-free.
steps.explain: Before 59½ it is usually income tax plus a 10% penalty. The Roth contribution rule does not apply to it.

steps.prompt: Which pile inside a Roth IRA is the one you can usually take out early without tax or penalty?
steps.explain: Contributions. Earnings wait on the age and five-year rules, aside from exceptions you should not build a budget on.

lessons.title: Maya Opens a Roth
lessons.summary: Under the limit, so the direct door.

story.title: The direct door
story.body:
Maya earned **$28,000** this year. That is under the 2026 Roth IRA income limit for a single filer.

She opens a Roth IRA, contributes **$1,500**, and buys a broad index fund. A backdoor is not her situation.

steps.title: Meet Maya
steps.body:
Maya is 22 and a library assistant. She earned $28,000 this year, which is under the 2026 Roth IRA income limit for a single filer. She has no IRA yet.

She opens a Roth IRA and puts in $1,500, then buys a broad [[index fund]]. She does not need a backdoor. $1,500 is under the $7,500 cap.

steps.prompt: Maya’s $28,000 income blocks a 2026 Roth IRA contribution.
steps.explain: $28,000 is far under $153,000. She can contribute, up to $7,500 and up to what she earned.

steps.prompt: How many dollars under the $7,500 cap is Maya’s $1,500 contribution?
steps.explain: $7,500 − $1,500 = $6,000 of room left. She does not have to fill it.

steps.prompt: What does Maya buy inside the new IRA?
choices: Her employer’s stock, because the fee is zero
steps.explain: The Roth IRA is the container. The fund is the investment.

steps.prompt: Put Maya’s afternoon in order.
items: Check that $28,000 is under the Roth income limit
steps.explain: The limit check first. Then the account, the money, and the fund.

lessons.title: Sharpen Up
lessons.summary: Smart repetition on what you’re closest to forgetting.

lessons.title: Den Trial: IRAs: Roth vs Traditional
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: At age 50 in 2026, what is the total IRA contribution limit including the catch-up?
Roth IRA contributions and Roth IRA earnings follow the same early-withdrawal rule.
steps.explain: Contributions can usually come out. Earnings generally wait on age 59½ and the five-year clock.

steps.prompt: A direct Roth IRA contribution is not allowed for a single filer in 2026 once modified AGI reaches what?
steps.explain: $168,000 or more blocks the direct contribution. $7,500 is the dollar cap. $24,500 is the 401(k) employee cap.

steps.prompt: You put $3,000 in a Roth IRA in 2026 and you are under 50. How many dollars of IRA room are left?
steps.explain: $7,500 − $3,000 = $4,500, shared with any traditional IRA contribution.
